name: 동굴 바닥을 가르는 한 칸 폭 깊은 틈 그물(위에서 본 3/4 지형 — 먼 벽 바위 낯·가까운 바닥 입술·옆벽 띠)
label: atlas_biome_interior/plus/abyss-c
reasons: 화풍: 칸 정보량이 기준보다 훨씬 낮음 (4/4)

surfaces.part: far-wall rock face with lit lip at top of each crevice (e.g. top crevice band)
near floor lip (light edge line below the dark gap)

answer.evidence: This is a terrain tile sheet of one-tile-wide crevices cut into a cave floor, not a standing object. Each crevice has a lit rock-face lip band (about rows 16-18 at x=128, light #8c7554) with a lighter edge line, then graded eave shadow (rows 19-23), then a deep black gap (rows 24-27), and a light near-floor lip line at row 28 (#ac9067). The same pattern repeats at rows 48-60 and 80-92. Vertical crevices show side-wall bands along their edges. The 3/4 structure is consistent: far wall face, dark depth, near floor lip. The floor is a flat top-down fill, which is correct for ground terrain.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has only 17 distinct colours against 80 in the grass reference. Its median is 5 colours per tile against 26 for grass and 7 for paving. The floor is a brown speckled soil with only about 3 lightness steps. The chasm interior is a near-flat black-brown gradient, and the lip is a thin tan strip with a dark edge and little per-pixel shading. Edge pixels are only 4% neutral, so the outlines lean brown and count as dark material tone. Flat-fill coverage is 4%, so the speckle does break up the floor. Even so, the shading ramps are shallow and the density is far below the grass reference. The crevice walls are barely modelled: there is no side-wall band with its own ramp, no rock-face texture and no stones shaded one by one. The piece reads as a simple, repeated soil texture with dark slots rather than a carefully layered 3/4 cave floor.

surfaces.part: far-wall rock face with lit top lip (chasm segments, e.g. horizontal chasm at top)
chasm interior (dark void) below the wall face
near floor lip at bottom edge of each chasm

answer.evidence: Terrain tile sheet: the floor is a flat top-down ground texture, and the crevices read in 3/4 view. Each chasm segment has a light top lip (rows 16-20 at x=191, 48-50 at x=64) that ends at a front-edge line, then a rock-face band with graded shading (L 120→92→69→49), then a near-black void (about 4 rows L=10), and a bright floor lip row (L=148, e.g. row 28, 60, 92) at the bottom. This is the far-wall rock face, void and near-floor lip structure the name describes. Vertical chasm segments show side-wall bands along their edges. Structure matches the terrain kind and has both a top lip and a visible face.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has only 17 distinct colours and a median of 5 per 16x16 tile. The grass reference has 80 colours and a median of 26, and even the paving reference reaches 7 per tile. The brown floor has some speckle grain, so flat-fill coverage is only 4%. The chasm interiors are nearly flat dark fills with 2-3 steps, and the tan lip is a thin one-pixel line with little step progression. The few dark edge pixels that exist are tinted brown (only 4% neutral), so the edges read as material tone and not a black sticker outline. The 3/4 depth reads weakly: the far-wall rock face is just a short gradient and the side-wall band has almost no per-stone shading. The ramps are too shallow against the 5-6 step Beodeul standard, and the density is far below the grass reference.

surfaces.part: floor lip and far rock wall of horizontal fissure (ground plane at top edge)
near floor lip below the chasm

answer.evidence: This is a terrain autotile block, not a standing object. The column scan at x=128 shows ground (rows 0-15), then a light lip line (rows 16-18, L=120, with a brighter edge pixel), then a brown rock-face gradient (rows 19-22), then a dark void (rows 23-27), then a light near-floor lip at row 28 and ground again. Each fissure shows the same sequence of top lip with front-edge line, shadowed vertical wall face, black depth, and near lip. The vertical fissures repeat this at the top with a lip and rock face, then a dark slot. Together these read as a 3/4 view with a top surface and a front face of about 9 rows.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has only 17 distinct colours and a median of 5 per tile. The grass reference has 80 colours and a median of 26, and the paving reference has a median of 7. The floor is a noisy brown speckle of about 4 browns, so it is not flat (flat-fill coverage is 4%), but it is a single repeated grain with no clumps, stones or larger-scale variation. The chasm interiors are mostly near-black with a thin gradient. The tan lip has a scalloped edge but only 2-3 tones, and the far rock face and side-wall band are barely distinguishable from the dark fill. Edges are tinted (only 4% neutral dark pixels), so they read as dark material tone rather than a sticker outline, and that part is fine. Overall the shading ramps are shallower and the colour variety much lower than the Beodeul grass reference, and the chasm reads as a dark fill rather than a modelled rock face. The paving reference is also sparse, but it still has more crafted per-stone shading than this candidate's chasm areas.

surfaces.part: cave floor ground plane (brown speckled tile)
far-wall rock face with near-floor lip bands over dark chasm (e.g. upper horizontal fissure)

answer.evidence: This is a terrain tile network: a full-bleed brown cave floor (256 wide on every row) cut by one-tile-wide dark fissures. Each fissure has a light lip line (about #ac9067 / #8c7554, 3 rows, e.g. rows 16-18 at x=128 and rows 48-50 at x=64) at the top. Below it are 2 rows of graded eave shadow, then 4 rows of near-black chasm (rows 24-27, 56-59), and a light near-floor lip line (rows 28, 60). The fissures read as a recessed gap with a far-wall rock face, a dark void and a near lip, in 3/4 view. Vertical fissures show side-wall bands along their edges. This is terrain, not a standing object, so the structure is consistent with a top-down 3/4 chasm.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has only 17 distinct colours and a median of 5 per 16x16 tile, against 26 and 80 for the grass reference. The paving reference is also low at 7 per tile, but it is a different, simpler material. The brown soil floor has grain speckle, and the 4% flat-fill coverage confirms there are no big flat areas. The crack walls are mostly a black gradient with a thin tan lip, so the ramp is shallow at about 3 steps for the chasm and about 3-4 for the soil, where the reference uses 5-6. The edges are tinted brown, not neutral (4% neutral), so they are dark material tone. The chasm interiors read as near-flat dark voids with little rock-face detail, and the far-wall rock face and side-wall band that the brief asks for are barely there. The lip is a single thin line with no per-stone shading. The maze-like layout is also repetitive. Next to the grass reference it looks thinner and simpler, with a low-variation soil texture and little tile-level information.
